title: Before anything, a voice (Genesis 1:1–5)
hookLine: the Torah opens "in the beginning" and speaks light into the dark

cards: No light. No ground. No sky.
The text calls it unformed and void: darkness over the deep, and a wind, or a spirit, hovering over the water. Nothing has happened yet, and nobody is there to see it.
Then, before any thing, before a single star, there's a sound. Someone speaks.

teach.b: The Torah's first word is Bereshit: in the beginning. It also names the whole book of Genesis, and the first weekly portion.
In the Jewish Publication Society's 1917 translation: "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth." Even that first word is argued over.

The medieval commentator Rashi pointed out that the grammar reads more like "in the beginning of God's creating," setting a scene rather than announcing the very first moment. Scholars still debate it.
The rabbis also noticed the first letter, bet.

It's closed on three sides and open only toward the front, the way Hebrew is read. One midrash calls that a hint: what came before, what's above and below, isn't yours to chase. Start here, and go forward.
Then the first thing God does isn't build or shape. It's speak.
"And God said: 'Let there be light.' And there was light." A sentence, and the world answers.
The Mishnah says the world was created with ten sayings. And the day closes: "And there was evening and there was morning, one day." Not the first day.
One day, with nothing yet to count against. So the Torah opens with the idea that words make things.

teach.h: DEATH AND LIFE ARE IN THE POWER OF THE TONGUE.
teach.b: The book of Proverbs says it plainly: "Death and life are in the power of the tongue."

how: Jews read Bereshit as the first weekly Torah portion each autumn, right after Simchat Torah, and the first chapter of Genesis is studied closely in Jewish learning.

games.q: you're a rabbi looking at the Torah's first letter, bet: closed on three sides, open toward the front. what does it teach?
o: the world is a closed box.
don't chase what came before; start here and go forward.
games.why: one midrash reads the bet this way: what's above, below and before isn't yours to chase. start from here, and go forward.

practice: Close your eyes and let it be dark for a moment, the way the story starts. Think of someone you'll talk to today, and find one kind sentence that's true of them: specific, not a compliment you'd give anybody.
When it's exactly right, say it once, softly, out loud.

wordCard.voice: Bereshit. In the beginning: the Torah's first word, where God speaks and light answers.

orig.note: Hebrew: in the beginning. the name of the first portion and of the book of Genesis.

carryVoice: Your line: words make worlds. The Torah's first act is a sentence. That's day twenty-two.
